subtopics.title: Introduction and Transport-Layer Services
subtopics.summary: Logical end-to-end communication between application processes on different hosts; the relationship between the transport and network layers and how the underlying network service model constrains transport services; overview of the Internet's transport protocols (UDP and TCP).

subtopics.title: Multiplexing and Demultiplexing
subtopics.summary: How the transport layer delivers segments to the correct application sockets using port numbers; connectionless (UDP) demultiplexing based on two-tuples versus connection-oriented (TCP) demultiplexing based on four-tuples.

subtopics.title: Connectionless Transport: UDP
subtopics.summary: UDP's minimal, no-frills service model, why applications choose it, its segment structure (header fields), and how the UDP checksum is computed and used for error detection.

subtopics.title: Principles of Reliable Data Transfer
subtopics.summary: Building a reliable channel over an unreliable network layer: ARQ with acknowledgments and retransmissions, sequence numbers, stop-and-wait versus pipelined operation, and the Go-Back-N (GBN) and Selective Repeat (SR) protocols.

subtopics.title: Connection-Oriented Transport: TCP
subtopics.summary: The TCP connection (three-way handshake and teardown), TCP segment structure, round-trip time estimation and timeout management, TCP's reliable data transfer mechanisms, and flow control with the receive window.

subtopics.title: Congestion Control
subtopics.summary: The causes and costs of network congestion, network-assisted versus end-to-end control approaches, and TCP's approach to congestion control (slow start, congestion avoidance/AIMD, fast recovery) along with fairness considerations.
